feedback.problem:
Find the values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for 
 $f(x)={x}^{2}$ on the interval $[-8,6].$
feedback.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[-8,6]$ and differentiable on $(-8,6).$ 

So, the mean value theorem states that there exists a $c\in (-8,6)$ such that

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.
$$

Plugging in $a=-8$ and $b=6$ into the above gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(c) & =\frac{f(6)-f(-8)}{6-(-8)} \\  & =\frac{{6}^{2}-(-8)^{2}}{14} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})=2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=2c.
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2c & =-2 \\ c & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
